summary.text: A 52-year-old man had PET-CT showing two hypermetabolic nodules suggestive of synchronous primary malignancies, one in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe (RS3) and one in RS6. He underwent dual-port video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy and RS6 segmentectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection and adhesiolysis; histopathology confirmed invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Chest radiography on postoperative day 2 showed satisfactory lung re-expansion, and the chest tube was removed.

Two hours after chest tube removal he developed acute profuse sweating, chest tightness and dyspnea without fever or pleuritic chest pain. Emergency chest radiography showed complete lung atelectasis and closed thoracic drainage yielded 200 mL of serous fluid. Multidetector CT with flexible bronchoscopy confirmed incomplete torsion of the right middle and lower lobes, with distal bronchial obstruction, an antler sign, maintained blood flow, bronchial torsion and stenosis, and a fish-mouth sign.

A multimodal conservative approach began with selective intrabronchial air insufflation every 48 hours, BiPAP three times daily for 2-hour sessions with continuous nasal cannula oxygen at 3 L/min between sessions, and maintained closed thoracic drainage, together with antibiotic prophylaxis and radiological monitoring. Operative intervention was deferred after informed consent discussions. After 3 days radiographs showed partial re-expansion; on postoperative day 7 three-dimensional imaging showed significant resolution of atelectasis and the chest tube was removed.

He stayed an additional 6 days for observation with an uncomplicated course and was discharged after confirmatory chest radiography. A three-month CT topogram showed complete re-expansion of the residual right lung, and at 2-year follow-up imaging showed sustained expansion without apparent long-term sequelae.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the four JPEG figures were inspected in the separate visual target.

Supplementary Material 1 is a procedure demonstration video (19 frames sampled every 2 s were viewed): protocol slides and bronchoscopy-room footage of a torsed bronchus; the article does not say the footage is this patient, so its slide parameters were not extracted as patient facts.
Supplementary Tables 1 (published cases) and 2 (proposed selection criteria) are literature or proposal content, not patient facts.
Discussion statements that early recognition prevented irreversible ischemic changes and that the approach gave superior outcomes are author interpretation and were not recorded as facts.
Caption of Figure 2B labels the emergency radiograph postoperative day 3 while the text places chest tube removal on postoperative day 2; kept as an ambiguity.
Pulmonary function test results are not reported; restoring pulmonary function is the authors statement only.
